m: Tokat Province (Turkish: Tokat ili) is a province in northern Turkey. Its area is 10,042 km2, and its population is 596,454 (2022). Its adjacent provinces are Amasya to the northwest, Yozgat to the southwest, Sivas to the southeast, and Ordu to the northeast. Its capital is Tokat, which lies inland of the middle Black Sea region, 422 kilometers from Ankara. The governor is Abdullah Köklü, appointed in 2024.

Q4852313:
Ballıca Cave (Turkish: Ballıca Mağarası) is a small cave situated 6 km (3.7 mi) southeast of Pazar, Tokat Province, Turkey. The cave is 600 m (2,000 ft) southeast of the Ballıca village.
Ballıca Cave is a fossil cave. Its overall length is 68 m (223 ft). The upper sections are composed of Permian–Triassic marble and lime. There are two layers above the entrance and five layers below, making a total of seven layers. Five layers were formed over three periods. One section stretches northeast and southwest, consisting of two layers. The second section, containing layers #3 and 34 were formed during the Second Evolutionary Period, and the 5th layer was formed in the 20th century. The gallery, which leads to some open space with a pond, is the first section in the northeast-southwest direction. It consists of the Stalactite and Stalagmite Hall on the first level, and the Fossil Hall and the Bat Hall on the second level. The Magnificent Gallery on the third floor is formed by three adjoining halls: the Mushroom, Column, and the New Hall. Dwarf bat colonies live in different parts of the cave and can be heard and smelled, but not often seen. The many colours in the cave are astonishing, and the filtered air is rich in oxygen.
About 45–50 m (148–164 ft) from the entrance, there is a wide saloon. The New Hall contains the remains (plastered walls, plastered material depot etc.) of use at some point in history. There are numerous stalactites, stalagmites, pillars and water ponds inside the saloon.
Q19605502:
Gökmedrese or Gök Medrese, is a 13th-century Anatolian Seljuk medrese, in Tokat, Turkey. It is dated to 1269-1270. The patron was Mu'in al-Din Suleyman (a vizier of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum).
The Gök Medrese is acknowledged for possibly the earliest known example of pure Mo'araq mosaic: complete inlaid cut-tilework with no intervening space between the tile fragments.
An example of Seljuk architecture, the building hosted for years the "Tokat Müzesi" (Museum of Tokat), an archaeological and ethnographical museum, until the latter moved in 2012 to a location in the bedesten area.
Q6099157:
Tokat Castle is an ancient citadel with 28 towers built on top of a rocky peak in the center of Tokat, Turkey.
While its first residents are unknown, the city's history dates back to 3,000 BC. The Hittites and Persians ruled over the area. The earliest known artifacts of the castle date back to the 5th century, and its first recorded residents were Christian groups migrating from Comana Pontica. The castle was under the control of the Byzantine Empire until its takeover by Danishmend Gazi in 1074 and eventual rule by the Great Seljuq Empire. It went through renovations in the Seljuq and Ottoman periods. Because it was used as a prison for rebels and government administrators at times, it was also called Çardar-ı Bedevi, meaning the Wild Arbor.
Vlad the Impaler (Dracula) was one of its inmates early in the 15th century when was he was imprisoned here for a short period by the Ottoman sultan Murad II. The castle is being restored and its secret passage is open to visitors.
Q54935354: Taşhan (Voyvoda Han) is a 17th-century Ottoman building on Gaziosmanpaşa Boulevard in the historic centre of Tokat.
Q21527391: Zile Castle stands on a mound in the centre of Zile, overlooking the Zile plain. Roman and Byzantine architectural pieces and inscriptions found in and around it suggest it was built in the 1st century AD.
Q2635905:
Gaziura, was a town in Pontus, on the river Iris, near the point where its course turns northwards. Some scholars equate Gaziura with Talaura, others with Ibora, and others with modern Turhal.
It was the ancient residence of the kings of Pontus, but in Strabo's time it was deserted. (Strab. xii.) Dion Cassius (xxxv. 12) notices it as a place where Mithridates VI of Pontus took up his position against the Roman Triarius. (Comp. Pliny vi. 2.)
Q6045228:
Ali Pasha Mosque (Turkish: Ali Paşa Camii) is a mosque in the centre of the town of Tokat in the Anatolia region of Turkey. It is a work of the Ottoman period, built in 1572 during the reign of Sultan Selim II, and has a single dome and a minaret.
It is part of complex which also includes a hamam (Turkish bathhouse) and a mausoleum. The tomb of Ali Pasha and his son Mustafa Bey is in the courtyard.
Q20668234: Hatuniye Complex (Turkish: Hatuniye Külliyesi) is a historical külliye, an Islamic religious complex, located in the city center of Tokat, Turkey. Its 1485 construction was ordered by Ottoman Sultan Bayezid II in honour of his mother, Gülbahar Hatun. Its facilities include a mosque, an imaret, and a medrese. At present, the mosque is used for prayer and other religious services, while the rest of the complex is open to visits by tourists and the public in general.
Q6032321: Tokat Museum is a museum in Tokat, Turkey. It houses historic finds from the region including sculptures and coins. Many of the items originate in the Anatolian Seljuks era.
Q6083081: Silahtar Ömer Pasha Mosque is in the town of Akça, Erbaa (Tokat). It was built of timber and cut stone using the çantı technique, without a single nail. It belongs to the General Directorate of Foundations and is still in use.
Q12812049: Takyeciler Mosque is on Sulu Sokak in Tokat, opposite the Yağıbasan Madrasa and next to the Arastalı Bedesten. It has no inscription naming its founder or date, but its plan, similar to multi-domed 15th-century Ottoman mosques, and the materials and form of its minaret base point to the 15th century.
Q97947316: Tokat Great Mosque is a mosque in Tokat.
Q118379638: Boyacı Hasan Ağa Mosque (Hızır Mosque) is a historic mosque in the centre of Zile, Tokat.
Q85793288:
Pida, or Pidae or Pidis, was a town of ancient Pontus, inhabited during Roman and Byzantine times. It was in the later province of Pontus Galaticus, on the road leading from Amasia to Neocaesareia.
Its site is located near Akça in Asiatic Turkey.
Q116051145: The Sen Timur Tomb is a 14th-century building in central Tokat, built as the tomb of the Mongol emir Nureddin bin Sentimur.
Q118958118: The Sultan Bath is in central Tokat.
Q115114296: Yağıbasan Madrasa, or Çukur Madrasa, was built in Tokat during the Danishmendid period.
Q116425431: Hatuniye Madrasa was built in 1485 by the Ottoman sultan Bayezid II in the name of his mother, Gülbahar Hatun. It stands next to the Hatuniye Mosque in the Meydan quarter of Tokat and, after restoration, is open to visitors. It is also known as the Sultaniye, Gülbahar or Meydan Madrasa.
Q116455520: Boğazkesen Bridge is a historic stone bridge in the Erbaa district of Tokat.
Q21527137: Tokat Clock Tower stands in central Tokat.
Q21528438: The Martyrs' Clock Tower, or Niksar Clock Tower, is in the Niksar district of Tokat. Built in 2008 by Mayor İdris Şahin, it bears the names of people from Niksar who died in the War of Independence and scenes from the war.
Q118946523: Hıdırlık Bridge is a Seljuk bridge in Tokat. It is said to have been built to reconcile İzzeddin, Rükneddin and Alaaddin, the three sons of Sultan Kaykhusraw, who had fought one another for three years. Built in 1250, it is still in use and stands where the eastern and southern caravan routes meet.
Q118958140: Leylekli Yılanlı Bridge is a historic bridge over the Çanakçı stream in the Niksar district of Tokat.
Q6000752: Lake Zinav (Sinan Lake) is a landslide-dammed lake in the Reşadiye district of Tokat. It is 1 km long, 70–500 m wide, up to 15 m deep and covers 26 hectares.
Q97321105: Kaz Gölü is a tectonic lake in Tokat province near the town of Üzümören on the Zile–Pazar road, on the Kazova plain in Turhal close to the Pazar district border.
Q6085378: The Melik Gazi Tomb is in the Kayapaşa quarter of Niksar, Tokat. Melik Danişmend Gümüştekin Ahmet Gazi, founder of the Danishmendids, conquered Niksar and made it both a base against the coastal Byzantines and his capital.
Q118957758: Zile Gül Mansion, formerly Tahir Efendi Mansion, is on Hacı Tahir Efendi Street in the Kislik quarter of Zile, Tokat. One of the finest examples of traditional architecture, it keeps its original design and carved woodwork in an intact historic street.
Q131901984: Turhal Castle in the Turhal district of Tokat is built on a steep rock about 180 m above the plain, commanding both the town and the plain. The Yeşilırmak river flows nearby.
Q6022474: Talazan Bridge crosses the Kelkit river 15 km from Niksar, Tokat. Talazan means 'sturdy, reliable'.
Q118957763: The Hacı Çıkrık Tomb is near the Çöreğibüyük Lodge in Niksar, Tokat. According to the inscription on its cenotaph base, it was built in 1182/1183 by Bedreddin Atabeg Ebu Mansur Şahinşah bin Arslan Doğmuş, one of Kılıç Arslan II's commanders. Its plan is nearly rectangular.
Q118958108: The Roman Arsenal in central Niksar, Tokat, was used as a military store in the Roman period; its architecture is dated to the 2nd–3rd century BC. Its floor is sealed with lime-based mortar, its ceiling has a ventilation shaft about 4 m high, the entrance has a brick vault and the walls are 1.2 m thick.
